Cancelled typescript concerning morphisms of toposes, their direct- and inverse-image functors, and transfer of algebraic structures. The document number is revised to 3.1.2; its top manuscript page number is read 22 with first-digit doubt against 72. Inverted archive 27 is recorded only as a comment. No date, title sheet, or total page count is visible.

The text says the inverse-image functor commutes with inductive limits and finite projective limits and is exact. It lists groups, rings, modules, comodules, bialgebras and torsors; ou de bimodule is locally cancelled.

The explicit hesitation is: "Plutôt que d'entrer dans la tâche peu engageante de donner un sens précis à cet énoncé et de le justifier de façon formelle". The inserted l'expliciter et de belongs to the advice to the reader. The cancelled vérifier que is not a surviving instruction.

C's source slips est muni and telles que celle de are retained. The final body fragment is se définis; no continuation is invented. The visible footnote has an open parenthesis after resp. à droite because the line is cut at the right edge.

H is an editorial synopsis, not a full diplomatic transcription. Its large omissions are listed as absences from this witness rather than claims that H misidentified each omitted word. Editorial guillemets in H are not copied as source quotation marks.

All ordinary typed E pairs were checked locally. The underlined E in objet de E' is distinct from them. The heavy lower impression on the later E is not silently treated as proof of a double-struck alphabet.

No mathematical issue triggered extra image views. Formula directions and adjunction consequences were checked only after the permitted image readings; uncertain reference numerals were not inferred from a theorem or another page.

No displays, commutative diagrams, or independent pictorial sketches occur. Graphic material consists of correction leaders, underlines, cancellation strokes, a divider, and the small extra traces preserved in reading.tex.
The complete reading.tex was saved before this report. No TeX compilation, OCR, external reference, other-page image, other-reader file, or second view of a decided image was used.
The low pale continuation of the page-wide trace, seen in the final-footnote crop, is drawn in gray as its own connected segment; its ink/surface status is left open.
